liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Me and My Uncle** (1 review): Jerry plays so fast on Uncle > Big River that he is ahead of Weir [27]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Garcia's middle solo in Estimated Prophet is particularly triumphant [22]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The performance of He's Gone is described as very emotional [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.5241.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 180 min [1]
- **gd1981-05-12.139954.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 168 min [2]
- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.chasingwilma.118987.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 180 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: The soundboard sounds great, featuring fine versions of Althea and Shakedown Street [23]
- **gd1981-05-12.149199.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1981-05-12.149198.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [6]. Said about its sound: The field recording holds up well under demands for thunderous volume [28]
- **gd1981-05-12.153022.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 173 min [7]
- **gd1981-05-12.mtx.seamons.99045.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 169 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [9]. Said about its sound: The sound is full, featuring crunchy organ on Little Red Rooster [30]
- **gd1981-05-12.123259.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [10]. Said about its sound: The recording has excellent sound, with sweet Roses and funky Althea [21]

## Around the show

- The band responded to the deaths of Bob Sands and Bob Marley with passionate playing [20]
- Jerry's guitar licks are admired, and Brent's playing is feverish and drives jams [20]
- He's Gone was dedicated to Bob Marley, and the set ended with high energy [21]
- Weir offered heartfelt words for Bob Marley before the Don't Ease Me In encore [22]
- He's Gone was dedicated to Bob Marley [23]
- The crowd noise is a significant positive aspect of the recording for this listener [24]
- He's Gone was dedicated to Bob Marley [7]
- This is a rare second set Looks Like Rain, as it was usually a first set song [26]
- The band is as hot as the May 1981 Nassau show, indicating a smokin' tour [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.5241.shnf**: taped by DAE(EAC) and SHN Encoding by Jeff M.; transferred by Upload and Tracking/SHN Encoding of d1t01,t02,t10 & t11 by; source: SBD>Master Cassette>Cassette>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd1981-05-12.139954.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (TDK MA90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) >… [2]
- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.chasingwilma.118987.flac16**: taped by chasingwilma; transferred by chasingwilma; source: Sbd> D-5> MC [4]
- **gd1981-05-12.149199.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM700 mics > Sony TC-D5M [5]. Also: Bob Wagner recorded; Miller transferred and coordinated; Jones assisted with pitch correction [5]
- **gd1981-05-12.149198.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM700 mics > Sony TC-D5M [6]
- **gd1981-05-12.153022.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi DM-500 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII) [7]. Also: Jim Vita recorded; Miller transferred; Wagner provided patches for Althea transition and Drums [7]
- **gd1981-05-12.mtx.seamons.99045.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [9]
- **gd1981-05-12.123259.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [10]

Bob Wagner recorded with Nak 700s in front of the board; Miller and Clugston transferred
The field recording holds up well under demands for thunderous volume
The sound is full, featuring crunchy organ on Little Red Rooster
Frank Streeter provided the master; Charlie Miller transferred the Nak 700 source
Bob Wagner recorded; Miller transferred and coordinated; Jones assisted with pitch correction
Jim Vita recorded; Miller transferred; Wagner provided patches for Althea transition and Drums
He's Gone was dedicated to Bob Marley
Jeff M. transferred SBD; JR Fishman handled AUD transfer and encoding; Seamons created matrix
